function: Centralized PPO agent jointly controls 3D positions, transmit and jamming power, and charging-station energy transfer of UAVs to maximize a secrecy-rate, energy-efficiency and interference utility (pp. 8-9).
system: Downlink from 10 transmitting UAVs to a ground center, 2 jamming UAVs, 1 eavesdropper; scalar channel gains, antennas not specified, no RIS; 2.4 GHz, 20 MHz (pp. 4-5, 10).
method: Single-agent PPO actor-critic (fully connected, 3 hidden layers of 64 neurons, GAE, clipped objective), reinforcement learning, centralized at the ground control center (pp. 8-11, Table 3).
data_channel: Simulated probabilistic LoS/NLoS air-to-ground path loss with small-scale fading at 2.4 GHz; 10 transmitting UAVs, 2 jammers, 1 eavesdropper in a 200 m area; no dataset (pp. 4-5, 10).
test_conditions: Training curves over 500 episodes in one simulated network; online test where the eavesdropper moves every 500 episodes, PPO re-converges by episode 514 versus 39 episodes initially (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: genetic algorithm (GA). Learned: DDPG similar to [28] and A3C similar to [52], [53] (p. 10).
metrics: Total utility, normalized total secrecy rate, energy utilization efficiency and total interference versus episode; episodes to convergence; percentage gains over DDPG and A3C (pp. 11-12).
complexity: Order O(2TM sum of C_in C_out) multiplications over T episodes and M time slots for the actor and critic networks; no runtime or FLOP figures (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "We adopt the widely used probabilistic model, as in [28]," for the LoS/NLoS air-to-ground path loss with small-scale fading; this is a custom simulator, not a 3GPP model, public dataset, or measurement.
q2_support: p. 12: "approximately 2.8 times faster than during initial training." after the eavesdropper relocates (re-converges by episode 514, versus "approximately 39 episodes to converge to a steady state." at the start): a reported adaptation to a changed condition using a fraction of the training effort.
q3_support: p. 10: "A conventional method, namely the genetic algorithm" and "A DRL-based method, specifically the DDPG algorithm" (also A3C); p. 11: "outperforms the DDPG and A3C algorithms by a utility" gap of 1.4 and 3.3, and "approximately 20.7 higher than those obtained by the GA".
q4_support: p. 10: "B. COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEXITY OF THE PPO MODEL" and "order of our proposed PPO model is expressed" as O(2TM times the sum of input and output neuron products).
q5_support: p. 10: "We simulate the UAV network scenario depicted in Fig. 1," a custom simulation; no public dataset or measured data is used and no link to code or data appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: PDF title and DOI match (p. 1). Tables 1-3 and Figs. 8-9 were read from the page images of pp. 4, 10, 11 and 13. Included because PPO learns transmit and jamming power and energy transfer jointly with UAV positions, and aerial-link power control passes the above_phy rule; area 6 admits single-antenna links and the antennas are never specified. The secrecy objective is not a listed exclusion, to be confirmed by the reviewer. q2 rests on the online re-adaptation to eavesdropper relocation (Fig. 9, p. 12); the reviewer should confirm that continued online learning counts as a reported adaptation. Table 2 prints the bandwidth as 20 MHz GHz.
